#000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:right;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;326,185&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:bottom;border-bottom:3px double #000000;background-color:#cceeff;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Leases&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We lease various offices, warehouses, equipment and vehicles. Rental contracts are typically made for fixed periods of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;15 years&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; but may have extension options. Lease terms are negotiated on an individual basis and contain a wide range of different terms and conditions. The lease agreements do not impose any covenants, but leased assets may not be used as security for borrowing purposes.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Up until the end of fiscal year 2019, leases of property, plant and equipment were classified as either finance or operating leases. Payments made under operating leases (net of any incentives received from the lessor) were charged to the income statement on a straight-line basis over the period of the lease (&#x201c;levelized lease cost&#x201d;).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Beginning October 1, 2019, leases are recognized as a right-of-use asset and a corresponding liability within accrued liabilities and other non-current liabilities at the date at which the leased asset is available for use by the Company. Each lease payment is allocated between the liability and finance cost. The finance cost is recognized over the lease period to produce a constant periodic rate of interest on the remaining balance of the liability for each period. The right-of-use asset is depreciated over the shorter of the asset's useful life and the lease term on a straight-line basis for finance type leases and as the difference between the levelized lease cost and the finance cost for operating leases. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:13px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Assets and liabilities arising from a lease are initially measured on a present value basis. Lease liabilities include the net present value of the following lease payments: &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Fixed payments (including in-substance fixed payments), less any lease incentives receivable&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Amounts expected to be payable by the lessee under residual value guarantees&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The exercise price of a purchase option if the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise that option, and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Payments of penalties for terminating the lease, if the lease term reflects the lessee exercising that option.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The lease payments are discounted using the interest rate implicit in the lease. If that rate cannot be determined, the lessee&#x2019;s incremental borrowing rate is used, which is the rate that the lessee would have to pay to borrow the funds necessary to obtain an asset of similar value in a similar economic environment with similar terms and conditions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:13px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Right-of-use assets are measured at cost and are comprised of the following:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The amount of the initial measurement of lease liability&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Any lease payments made at or before the commencement date less any lease incentives received&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Any initial direct costs, and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Asset retirement obligations related to that lease, as applicable.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Payments associated with short-term leases and leases of low-value assets are recognized on a straight-line basis as an expense in profit or loss. Short-term leases are leases with a lease term of 12 months or less. Low-value assets are comprised of IT-equipment and office furniture.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;In determining the lease term, management considers all facts and circumstances that create an economic incentive to exercise an extension option, or not exercise a termination option. Extension options (or periods after termination options) are only included in the lease term if the lease is reasonably certain to be extended (or not terminated). The assessment is reviewed if a significant event or a significant change in circumstances occurs and is within the control of the lessee. Refer to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Note 6&#x2014;Leases &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;for additional information regarding our leases. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Recently Issued Accounting Updates&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Changes to U.S. GAAP are established by the Financial Accounting Standards Board ("FASB") in the form of Accounting Standards Updates ("ASUs") to the FASB Accounting Standards Codification ("ASC"). We consider the applicability and impact of all ASUs. #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;ASU No. 2016-02 requires organizations that lease assets &#x2014; Lessor accounting remains substantially similar to current U.S. GAAP. In addition, disclosures of leasing activities are to be expanded to include qualitative along with specific quantitative information. ASU No. 2016-02 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2018, including interim periods within those fiscal years. ASU 2016-02 mandates a modified retrospective transition method of adoption with an option to use certain practical expedients.&#160;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;October 1, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;We adopted this ASU during the first quarter of fiscal year 2020, as required. Refer to Note 6&#x2014;Leases for additional information. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;ASU No. 2018-15, Intangibles - Goodwill and Other - Internal Use Software (Subtopic 350-40): Customer's Accounting for Implementation Costs Incurred in a Cloud Computing Arrangement That is a Service Contract&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;This ASU aims to reduce complexity in the accounting for costs of implementing a cloud computing service arrangement. Early adoption of the amendment is permitted, including adoption in any interim period for public entities for periods for which financial statements have not yet been issued.  An entity that elects to early adopt the amendments in an interim period should reflect any adjustments as of the beginning of the annual period that includes that interim period.  Additionally, an entity that elects early adoption must adopt all the amendments in the same period.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;October 1, 2021&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;We are currently evaluating the impact the new guidance may have on our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and disclosures.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Self-Insurance&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We self-insure a significant portion of expected losses relating to workers&#x2019; compensation, general liability and automobile liability. Generally, deductibles range from &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$1 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$10 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; per occurrence depending on the coverage and whether a claim occurs outside or inside of the United States. Insurance is purchased over deductibles to reduce our exposure to catastrophic events. Estimates are recorded for incurred outstanding liabilities for workers&#x2019; compensation, general liability claims and claims that are incurred but not reported. Estimates are based on adjusters' estimates, historical experience and statistical methods commonly used within the insurance industry that we believe are reliable.&#160;We have also engaged a third-party actuary to perform a review of our domestic casualty losses as well as losses in our captive insurance companies.&#160;Nonetheless, insurance estimates include certain assumptions and management judgments regarding the frequency and severity of claims, claim development and settlement practices. Unanticipated changes in these factors may produce materially different amounts of expense that would be reported under these programs.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;On October 1, 2019, we elected to utilize a wholly owned insurance captive (&#x201c;Captive&#x201d;) to insure the deductibles for our workers&#x2019; compensation, general liability and automobile liability insurance programs. Casualty claims occurring prior to October 1, 2019 will remain on the operating segment books and future adjustments to these claims will continue to be reflected within the operating segments. Reserves for legacy claims occurring prior to October 1, 2019, will remain as liabilities in our operating segments until they have been resolved. Changes in those reserves will be reflected in segment earnings as they occur. We also intend to continue utilizing the Captive to insure the deductibles for our assets under a property insurance program. The Company and the Captive maintain excess property and casualty reinsurance programs with third-party insurers in an effort to limit the financial impact of significant events covered under these programs. Our operating subsidiaries are paying premiums to the Captive, typically on a monthly basis, for the estimated losses based on the external actuarial analysis. These premiums are held in a restricted account, resulting in a transfer of risk from our operating subsidiaries to the Captive for the deductible self-insurance retention. The actuarial estimated underwriting expenses for the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three and six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; was approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$6.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$14.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively, and was recorded within Contract drilling services operating expenses in our Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations. Intercompany premium revenues and expenses during the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three and six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; amounted to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$10.5 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$18.2 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively, which were eliminated upon consolidation.&#160;These intercompany insurance premiums are reflected as segment operating expenses within the U.S. Land, Offshore, and International Land reportable operating segments and are reflected as intersegment sales within "Other". The Company previously self-insured employee health plan exposures in excess of employee deductibles. Starting in the second quarter of fiscal year &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Captive insurer issued a stop-loss program that will pay for health plan claims that exceed &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$50,000&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. One hundred percent of the stop-loss premium is being set aside by the Captive as reserves.  The stop-loss program does not have a material impact on a consolidated basis.&#160; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;"&gt;International Land Drilling Risks&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;International Land drilling operations may significantly contribute to our revenues and net operating income.&#160;There can be no assurance that we will be able to successfully conduct such operations, and a failure to do so may have an adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations, and cash flows.&#160;Also, the success of our international land operations will be subject to numerous contingencies, some of which are beyond management&#x2019;s control.&#160;These contingencies include general and regional economic conditions, fluctuations in currency exchange rates, modified exchange controls, changes in international regulatory requirements and international employment issues, risk of expropriation of real and personal property and the burden of complying with foreign laws.&#160;Additionally, in the event that extended labor strikes occur or a country experiences significant political, economic or social instability, we could experience shortages in labor and/or material and supplies necessary to operate some of our drilling rigs, thereby potentially causing an adverse material effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations. In Argentina, while our dayrate is denominated in U.S. dollars, we are paid in Argentine pesos.&#160;The Argentine branch of one of our second-tier subsidiaries remits U.S. dollars to its U.S. parent by converting the Argentine pesos into U.S. dollars through the Argentine Foreign Exchange Market and repatriating the U.S. dollars.&#160;Argentina also has a history of implementing currency controls which restrict the conversion and repatriation of U.S. dollars, including controls that were implemented in September 2019 and are presently in effect. As a result of these currency controls, our ability to remit funds from our Argentine subsidiary to its U.S. parent has been limited. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, our cash balance in Argentina was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$33.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;In the past the Argentine government has also instituted price controls on crude oil, diesel and gasoline prices and instituted an exchange rate freeze in connection with those prices. These price controls and an exchange rate freeze could be instituted again in the future. Argentina&#x2019;s economy is considered highly inflationary, which is defined as cumulative inflation rates exceeding &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;100 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in the most recent three-year period based on inflation data published by the respective governments.&#160;Nonetheless, all of our foreign subsidiaries use the U.S. dollar as the functional currency and local currency monetary assets and liabilities are remeasured into U.S. dollars with gains and losses resulting from foreign currency transactions included in current results of operations.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;For the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three and six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, we experienced aggregate foreign currency &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;losses&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$3.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.8 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively. For the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three and six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, we recorded aggregate foreign currency losses of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$0.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$4.6 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.     <us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2020Q2YTD"
      id="TextSelection-A8F56C612A6D5901864E273CE17DFBAC-0-wk-Fact-A9DFFAD03F9D546B94872CE4CE9635AF">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Leases&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We lease various offices, warehouses, equipment and vehicles. Rental contracts are typically made for fixed periods of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;15 years&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; but may have extension options. Lease terms are negotiated on an individual basis and contain a wide range of different terms and conditions. The lease agreements do not impose any covenants, but leased assets may not be used as security for borrowing purposes.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Up until the end of fiscal year 2019, leases of property, plant and equipment were classified as either finance or operating leases. Payments made under operating leases (net of any incentives received from the lessor) were charged to the income statement on a straight-line basis over the period of the lease (&#x201c;levelized lease cost&#x201d;).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Beginning October 1, 2019, leases are recognized as a right-of-use asset and a corresponding liability within accrued liabilities and other non-current liabilities at the date at which the leased asset is available for use by the Company. Each lease payment is allocated between the liability and finance cost. The finance cost is recognized over the lease period to produce a constant periodic rate of interest on the remaining balance of the liability for each period. The right-of-use asset is depreciated over the shorter of the asset's useful life and the lease term on a straight-line basis for finance type leases and as the difference between the levelized lease cost and the finance cost for operating leases. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:13px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Assets and liabilities arising from a lease are initially measured on a present value basis. font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The exercise price of a purchase option if the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise that option, and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; If that rate cannot be determined, the lessee&#x2019;s incremental borrowing rate is used, which is the rate that the lessee would have to pay to borrow the funds necessary to obtain an asset of similar value in a similar economic environment with similar terms and conditions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:13px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Right-of-use assets are measured at cost and are comprised of the following:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; Short-term leases are leases with a lease term of 12 months or less. Low-value assets are comprised of IT-equipment and office furniture.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;In determining the lease term, management considers all facts and circumstances that create an economic incentive to exercise an extension option, or not exercise a termination option. Extension options (or periods after termination options) are only included in the lease term if the lease is reasonably certain to be extended (or not terminated). #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;ASU No. 2016-02, Leases (Topic 842) and related ASUs issued subsequent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;ASU No. 2016-02 requires organizations that lease assets &#x2014; referred to as &#x201c;lessees&#x201d; &#x2014; to recognize on the balance sheet the assets and liabilities for the rights and obligations created by those leases with lease terms of more than 12 months. Lessor accounting remains substantially similar to current U.S. GAAP. In addition, disclosures of leasing activities are to be expanded to include qualitative along with specific quantitative information. ASU No. 2016-02 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2018, including interim periods within those fiscal years. ASU 2016-02 mandates a modified retrospective transition method of adoption with an option to use certain practical expedients.&#160;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;October 1, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;We adopted this ASU during the first quarter of fiscal year 2020, as required. Refer to Note 6&#x2014;Leases for additional information. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;ASU No. 2018-15, Intangibles - Goodwill and Other - Internal Use Software (Subtopic 350-40): Customer's Accounting for Implementation Costs Incurred in a Cloud Computing Arrangement That is a Service Contract&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;This ASU aims to reduce complexity in the accounting for costs of implementing a cloud computing service arrangement. ASU No. 2018-15 aligns the requirements for capitalizing implementation costs incurred in a hosting arrangement that is a service contract with the requirements for capitalizing implementation costs incurred to develop or obtain internal-use software (and hosting arrangements that include an internal-use software license). This update is effective for annual and interim periods beginning after December 15, 2019. The amendments in this update should be applied either retrospectively or prospectively to all implementation costs incurred after the date of adoption.  Early adoption is permitted.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;October 1, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;We early adopted this ASU during the first quarter of fiscal year 2020 on a prospective basis. The prospective impact was not material to our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and disclosures. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td colspan="4" style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#acacac;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Standards that are not yet adopted as of March 31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;ASU No. 2016-13, Financial Instruments &#x2013; Credit Losses (Topic 326) and related ASUs issued subsequent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;This ASU introduces a new model for recognizing credit losses on financial instruments based on an estimate of current expected credit losses. The new model will apply to: (1) loans, accounts receivable, trade receivables, and other financial assets measured at amortized cost, (2) loan commitments and certain other off-balance sheet credit exposures, (3) debt securities and other financial assets measured at fair value through other comprehensive income(loss), and (4) beneficial interests in securitized financial assets. This update is effective for annual and interim periods beginning after December 15, 2019. &#160; &#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;October 1, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;We are currently evaluating the impact the new guidance may have on our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and disclosures.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;background-color:;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;ASU No. 2018-14, Compensation &#x2013; In Argentina, while our dayrate is denominated in U.S. dollars, we are paid in Argentine pesos.&#160;The Argentine branch of one of our second-tier subsidiaries remits U.S. dollars to its U.S. parent by converting the Argentine pesos into U.S. dollars through the Argentine Foreign Exchange Market and repatriating the U.S. dollars.&#160;Argentina also has a history of implementing currency controls which restrict the conversion and repatriation of U.S. dollars, including controls that were implemented in September 2019 and are presently in effect. As a result of these currency controls, our ability to remit funds from our Argentine subsidiary to its U.S. parent has been limited. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, our cash balance in Argentina was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$33.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;In the past the Argentine government has also instituted price controls on crude oil, diesel and gasoline prices and instituted an exchange rate freeze in connection with those prices. These price controls and an exchange rate freeze could be instituted again in the future. Argentina&#x2019;s economy is considered highly inflationary, which is defined as cumulative inflation rates exceeding &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;100 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in the most recent three-year period based on inflation data published by the respective governments.&#160;Nonetheless, all of our foreign subsidiaries use the U.S. dollar as the functional currency and local currency monetary assets and liabilities are remeasured into U.S. dollars with gains and losses resulting from foreign currency transactions included in current results of operations.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;For the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three and six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, we experienced aggregate foreign currency &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;losses&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$3.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.8 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively. For the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three and six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, we recorded aggregate foreign currency losses of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$0.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$4.6 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively. In the future, we may incur larger currency devaluations, foreign exchange restrictions or other difficulties repatriating U.S. dollars from Argentina or elsewhere, which could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Because of the impact of local laws, our future operations in certain areas may be conducted through entities in which local citizens own interests and through entities (including joint ventures) in which we hold only a minority interest or pursuant to arrangements under which we conduct operations under contract to local entities.&#160;While we believe that neither operating through such entities nor pursuant to such arrangements would have a material adverse effect on our operations or revenues, there can be no assurance that we will in all cases be able to structure or restructure our operations to conform to local law (or the administration thereof) on terms acceptable to us.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Although we attempt to minimize the potential impact of such risks by operating in more than &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;one&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; These gains were primarily related to reimbursement for drill pipe damaged or lost in drilling operations. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Impairments&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Consistent with our policy, we evaluate our drilling rigs and related equipment for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying value of these assets may exceed the estimated undiscounted future net cash flows. Our evaluation, among other things, includes a review of external market factors and an assessment on the future marketability of a specific rigs&#x2019; asset group. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the three months ended March 31, 2020, several significant economic events took place that severely impacted the current demand on drilling services, including the significant drop in crude oil prices caused by OPEC+'s price war coupled with a decrease in the demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;To maintain a competitive edge in a challenging market, the Company&#x2019;s management introduced a new strategy focused on operating various types of highly capable upgraded rigs and phasing out the older, less capable fleet. This resulted in grouping the super-spec rigs of our legacy Domestic FlexRig3 asset group with our FlexRig5 asset group creating a new "Domestic super-spec FlexRig" asset group, while combining the legacy Domestic conventional asset group, FlexRig4 asset group  and FlexRig3 non-super-spec rigs into one asset group (Domestic non-super-spec asset group)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; (See &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Note 18&#x2014;Subsequent Events&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;).  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Given the current and projected low utilization for our Domestic non-super-spec asset group and all International asset groups, we considered these economic factors to be indicators that these asset groups may be impaired.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"/&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;At March 31, 2020, we performed impairment testing on our Domestic non-super-spec and International conventional, FlexRig3, and FlexRig4 asset groups which had an aggregate net book value of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$605.8 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We concluded that the net book value of each asset group is not recoverable through estimated undiscounted cash flows and recorded a non-cash impairment charge of&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$441.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in the Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations during the three and six months ended March 31, 2020. Of the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$441.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;total impairment charge recorded, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$292.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$149.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;was recorded in the U.S. Land and International Land segment, respectively. Impairment was measured as the amount by which the net book value of each asset group exceeds its fair value.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"/&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The most significant assumptions used in our undiscounted cash flow model include timing on awards of future drilling contracts, drilling rig utilization, estimated remaining useful life, and net proceeds received upon future sale/disposition. These assumptions are classified as Level 3 inputs by ASC Topic 820 Fair Value measurement and Disclosures as they are based upon unobservable inputs and primarily rely on management assumptions and forecasts.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:7pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"/&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;In determining the fair value of each asset group, we utilized a combination of income and market approaches. The significant assumptions in the valuation are based on those of a market participant and are classified as Level 2 and Level 3 inputs by ASC Topic 820 Fair Value Measurement and Disclosures.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"/&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company also recorded an additional non-cash impairment charge related to in-progress drilling equipment and rotational inventory of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$44.9 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$38.6 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively, which had aggregate book values of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$68.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$38.6 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively, in the Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations during the three and six months ended March 31, 2020. Of the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$83.5 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;total impairment charge recorded for in-progress drilling equipment and rotational inventory,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$75.8 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$7.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;was recorded in the U.S. Land and International Land segment, respectively.&lt;/span&gt;</us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentDisclosureTextBlock>

The reclassifications and the adjustments arising from the new leasing rules are therefore recognized in the opening balance sheet on October 1, 2019.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Upon adoption of ASC 842, we recognized lease liabilities in relation to leases that had previously been classified as operating leases under the principles of ASC 840. These liabilities were measured at the present value of the remaining lease payments, discounted using the lessee&#x2019;s incremental borrowing rate as of October 1, 2019, as most of our contracts do not provide an implicit rate. Additionally, ASC 842 provides lessors with a practical expedient, by class of underlying asset, to not separate lease and non-lease components and account for the combined component under ASC 606 when the non-lease component is the predominant element of the combined component. The lessor practical expedient is limited to circumstances in which the lease, if accounted for separately, would be classified as an operating lease under ASC 842.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;With respect to our drilling service contracts that commenced or were amended during the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;six months ended March 31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, we concluded that our drilling contracts contain a lease component and that the non-lease component is the predominant element of the combined component of such contracts. As such, we elected to apply the practical expedient to not separate the lease and non-lease components and account for the combined component under ASC 606. Therefore, we do not expect any change in our revenue recognition patterns or disclosures as a result of our adoption of ASC 842.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div Due to the market conditions described in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;Note 5&#x2014;Property, Plant and Equipment&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;, we concluded that goodwill and intangible assets might be impaired and tested the H&amp;amp;P Technologies reporting unit, where the goodwill balance is allocated and the intangible assets are recorded, for recoverability.  This resulted in a goodwill only non-cash &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;impairment charge of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$38.3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; recorded in Asset Impairment Charge on the Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations during the three and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;six months ended March 31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;The recoverable amount of the H&amp;amp;P Technologies segment as a reporting unit is determined based on a fair value calculation which uses cash flow projections based on the Company&#x2019;s financial budgets approved by the board of directors covering a five-year period, and a discount rate of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;14 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;. Cash flows beyond that five-year period have been extrapolated using the fifth-year data with no implied growth factor. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The recoverable amount of the intangible assets tested for impairment within the H&amp;amp;P Technologies reporting unit is determined based on undiscounted cash flow projections using the Company&#x2019;s financial budgets approved by the board of directors covering a five-year period, and extrapolated for the remaining weighted average useful lives of the intangible assets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;The most significant assumptions used in our cash flow model include timing on awards of future contracts, commercial pricing terms, utilization, discount rate, and the terminal value. These assumptions are classified as Level 3 inputs by ASC Topic 820 Fair Value Measurement and Disclosures as they are based upon unobservable inputs and primarily rely on management assumptions and forecasts. Although we believe the assumptions used in our analysis and the probability-weighted average of expected future cash flows are reasonable and appropriate, different assumptions and estimates could materially impact the analysis and our resulting conclusion.</us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsDisclosureTextBlock>

On &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&#160;20, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, HPIDC, the Company and Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as trustee, entered into a supplemental indenture to the indenture governing the HPIDC 2025 Notes to adopt certain proposed amendments pursuant to a consent solicitation conducted concurrently with the Exchange Offer.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;On September 27, 2019, we redeemed the remaining approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$12.9 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in aggregate principal amount of HPIDC 2025 Notes for approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$14.6 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, including accrued interest and a prepayment premium. Simultaneously with the redemption of the HPIDC 2025 Notes, HPIDC was released as a guarantor under the Company 2025 Notes and the 2018 Credit Facility (as defined herein). As a result of such release, H&amp;amp;P is the only obligor under the Company 2025 Notes and the 2018 Credit Facility.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Credit Facilities&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;On November 13, 2018, we entered into a credit agreement by and among the Company, as borrower, Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as administrative agent, and the lenders party thereto, providing for an unsecured revolving credit facility (as amended, the &#x201c;2018 Credit Facility&#x201d;), which is set to mature on November 13, 2024. The 2018 Credit Facility has &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$750 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in aggregate availability with a maximum of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$75 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; available for use as letters of credit. The 2018 Credit Facility also permits aggregate commitments under the facility to be increased by &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$300 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions and the procurement of additional commitments from new or existing lenders. The borrowings under the 2018 Credit Facility accrue interest at a spread over either the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) or the Base Rate. We also pay a commitment fee on the unused balance of the facility. Borrowing spreads as well as commitment fees are determined based on the debt rating for senior unsecured debt of the Company, as determined by Moody&#x2019;s and Standard &amp;amp; Poor&#x2019;s. The spread over LIBOR ranges from &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;0.875 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;1.500 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; per annum and commitment fees range from &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;0.075 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;0.200 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; per annum. There is a financial covenant in the 2018 Credit Facility that requires us to maintain a total debt to total capitalization ratio of less than or equal to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;50 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. The 2018 Credit Facility contains additional terms, conditions, restrictions and covenants that we believe are usual and customary in unsecured debt arrangements for companies of similar size and credit quality, including a limitation that priority debt (as defined in the credit agreement) may not exceed &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;17.5 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of the net worth of the Company. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, there were &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;no&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; borrowings or letters of credit outstanding, leaving &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$750.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; available to borrow under the 2018 Credit Facility. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, we had &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;two&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; outstanding letters of credit with banks, in the amounts of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$24.8 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.1 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, we also had a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$20.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; unsecured standalone line of credit facility, for the purpose of obtaining the issuance of international letters of credit, bank guarantees, and performance bonds. Of the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$20.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$14.3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of financial guarantees were outstanding as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The applicable agreements for all unsecured debt contain additional terms, conditions and restrictions that we believe are usual and customary in unsecured debt arrangements for companies that are similar in size and credit quality.&#160;&#160;At &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;we were in compliance with all debt covenants&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:DebtDisclosureTextBlock>

In calculating our estimated annual effective tax rate, we consider forecasted annual pre-tax income and estimated permanent book versus tax differences. Adjustments to the effective tax rate and estimates will occur as information and assumptions change.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Our income tax &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;(benefit)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; provision from continuing operations for the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three months ended March 31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$(113.4) million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$25.1 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively, resulting in effective tax rates of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;21.2 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;25.9 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively. Our income tax provision &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;(benefit)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; from continuing operations for the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;six months ended March 31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$(99.3) million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$26.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively, resulting in effective tax rates of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;20.3 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;24.8 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively. style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Performance Share Units&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We have made awards to certain employees that are subject to market-based performance conditions ("performance share units"). Subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the applicable performance share unit award agreements and the 2016 Plan, grants of performance share units are subject to a vesting period of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;three years&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; (the &#x201c;Vesting Period&#x201d;) that is dependent on the achievement of certain performance goals. Such performance share unit awards consist of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;two&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; separate components.&#160;Performance share units that comprise the first component are subject to a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-year performance cycle.&#160;Performance share units that comprise the second component are further divided into &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; separate tranches, each of which is subject to a separate &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;one&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-year performance cycle within the full &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-year performance cycle.&#160;&#160;The vesting of the performance share units is generally dependent on (i) the achievement of the Company&#x2019;s total shareholder return (&#x201c;TSR&#x201d;) performance goals relative to the TSR achievement of a peer group of companies (the &#x201c;Peer Group&#x201d;) over the applicable performance cycle, and (ii) the continued employment of the recipient of the performance share unit award throughout the Vesting Period.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;At the end of the Vesting Period, recipients receive dividend equivalents, if any, with respect to the number of vested performance share units. The vesting of units ranges from &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;zero&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;200 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of the units granted depending on the Company&#x2019;s TSR relative to the TSR of the Peer Group on the vesting date.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The grant date fair value of performance share units was determined through use of the Monte Carlo simulation method. The Monte Carlo simulation method requires the use of highly subjective assumptions. Our key assumptions in the method include the price and the expected volatility of our stock and our self-determined Peer Group companies&#x2019; stock, risk free rate of return and cross-correlations between the Company and our Peer Group companies. The valuation model assumes dividends are immediately reinvested. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, there was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$11.6 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of unrecognized compensation cost related to unvested performance share units. style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and changes in non-vested performance share units outstanding during the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span
