<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:none;">NOTE 16 COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:none;"> </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Purchase Commitments</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Equipment, parts and supplies are ordered in advance to promote efficient construction and capital improvement progress.&#160;At </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we had purchase commitments for equipment, parts and supplies of approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$12.7 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Lease Obligations</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Refer to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:normal;">Note 6&#8212;Leases </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">for additional information on our lease obligations. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Guarantee Arrangements</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We are contingently liable to sureties in respect of bonds issued by the sureties in connection with certain commitments entered into by us in the normal course of business.&#160;&#160;We have agreed to indemnify the sureties for any payments made by them in respect of such bonds.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Contingencies</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">During the ordinary course of our business, contingencies arise resulting from an existing condition, situation or set of circumstances involving an uncertainty as to the realization of a possible gain or loss contingency.&#160; We account for gain contingencies in accordance with the provisions of ASC 450, Contingencies, and, therefore, we do not record gain contingencies or recognize income until realized.&#160; The property and equipment of our Venezuelan subsidiary was seized by the Venezuelan government on June&#160;30, 2010.&#160; HPIDC, our wholly-owned subsidiary and the parent company of our Venezuelan subsidiary, has a lawsuit pending in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia against the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, Petroleos de Venezuela, S.A. and PDVSA Petroleo, S.A.,&#160;seeking damages for the taking of their Venezuelan drilling business in violation of international law.&#160; While there exists the possibility of realizing a recovery, we are currently unable to determine the timing or amounts we may receive, if any, or the likelihood of recovery.&#160;</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">In October 2017, an employee of HPIDC suffered personal injury and subsequently brought a lawsuit against the operator.  Pursuant to the terms of the drilling contract between HPIDC and the operator, HPIDC indemnified the operator in the lawsuit, subject to certain limitations. A settlement agreement was reached with the operator.  As of September 30, 2019, we accrued </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$9.5 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> for this lawsuit, which was subsequently paid out during the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">six months ended March 31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. The Company and its subsidiaries are parties to various other pending legal actions arising in the ordinary course of our business.&#160;We maintain insurance against certain business risks subject to certain deductibles.&#160;&#160;Although no assurance can be given, we believe, based on our experiences to date and taking into account established reserves and insurance, that the ultimate resolution of such items will not have a material adverse impact on our financial condition, cash flows, or results of operations.&#160;When we determine a loss is probable of occurring and is reasonably estimable, we accrue an undiscounted liability for such contingencies based on our best estimate using information available at that time.&#160;&#160;If the estimated loss is a range of potential outcomes and there is no better estimate within the range, we accrue the amount at the low end of the range.&#160;&#160;We disclose contingencies where an adverse outcome may be material, or in the judgment of management, we conclude the matter should otherwise be disclosed.</span></div><span></span>
</td>

<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:none;">NOTE 4 DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"> </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Current and noncurrent liabilities from discontinued operations consist of municipal and income taxes payable and social obligations due within the country of Venezuela.&#160;Expenses incurred for in-country obligations are reported as discontinued operations within our Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations.&#160;</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The activity for the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">three and six</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> was primarily due to the remeasurement of uncertain tax liabilities as a result of the devaluation of the Venezuela Bolivar.&#160; Early in 2018, the Venezuelan government announced that it changed the existing dual-rate foreign currency exchange system by eliminating its heavily subsidized foreign exchange rate, which was </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>10</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> Bolivars per United States dollar, and relaunched an exchange system known as DICOM.&#160;The Venezuela government also established a new currency called the &#8220;Sovereign Bolivar,&#8221; which was determined by the elimination of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>five</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> zeros from the old currency. The DICOM floating rate was approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>80,946</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> Bolivars per United States dollar at </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;The DICOM floating rate might not reflect the barter market exchange rates.</span></div><span></span>

style="vertical-align:bottom;border-bottom:3px double #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;"><div style="text-align:right;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"><span>(7,792</span></span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:bottom;border-bottom:3px double style="vertical-align:bottom;border-bottom:3px double #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;"><div style="text-align:right;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"><span>479,356</span></span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:bottom;border-bottom:3px double #000000;background-color:#cceeff;"><div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div></td></tr></table></div><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Senior Notes</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">HPIDC 2025 Notes</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">On March 19, 2015, our subsidiary, Helmerich &amp; Payne International Drilling Co. </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">("HPIDC") issued </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$500 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>4.65 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> unsecured senior notes due 2025 of HPIDC (the "HPIDC 2025 Notes"), which were redeemed in full on September 27, 2019 as described under "&#8211;&#8211;Exchange Offer, Consent Solicitation and Redemption."&#160;Interest on the HPIDC 2025 Notes was payable semi-annually on March 15 and September 15.&#160;The debt discount was being amortized to interest expense using the effective interest method.&#160;The debt issuance costs were being amortized straight-line over the stated life of the obligation, which approximated the effective interest method.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Exchange Offer, Consent Solicitation and Redemption</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">On </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;20, 2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we settled an offer to exchange (the &#8220;Exchange Offer&#8221;) any and all outstanding HPIDC 2025 Notes for (i) up to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$500 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> aggregate principal amount of new </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>4.65 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> unsecured senior notes due 2025 of the Company (the &#8220;Company 2025 Notes&#8221;), with registration rights, and (ii) cash, pursuant to which we issued approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$487.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> in aggregate principal amount of Company 2025 Notes. Interest on the Company 2025 Notes is payable semi-annually on March 15 and September 15 of each year, commencing March 15, 2019. The debt issuance costs are being amortized straight-line over the stated life of the obligation, which approximates the effective interest method. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Following the consummation of the Exchange Offer, HPIDC had outstanding approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$12.9 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> in aggregate principal amount of HPIDC 2025 Notes. On </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;20, 2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, HPIDC, the Company and Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as trustee, entered into a supplemental indenture to the indenture governing the HPIDC 2025 Notes to adopt certain proposed amendments pursuant to a consent solicitation conducted concurrently with the Exchange Offer.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">On September 27, 2019, we redeemed the remaining approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$12.9 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> in aggregate principal amount of HPIDC 2025 Notes for approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$14.6 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, including accrued interest and a prepayment premium. Simultaneously with the redemption of the HPIDC 2025 Notes, HPIDC was released as a guarantor under the Company 2025 Notes and the 2018 Credit Facility (as defined herein). As a result of such release, H&amp;P is the only obligor under the Company 2025 Notes and the 2018 Credit Facility.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Credit Facilities</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">On November 13, 2018, we entered into a credit agreement by and among the Company, as borrower, Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as administrative agent, and the lenders party thereto, providing for an unsecured revolving credit facility (as amended, the &#8220;2018 Credit Facility&#8221;), which is set to mature on November 13, 2024. The 2018 Credit Facility has </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$750 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> in aggregate availability with a maximum of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$75 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> available for use as letters of credit. The 2018 Credit Facility also permits aggregate commitments under the facility to be increased by </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$300 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions and the procurement of additional commitments from new or existing lenders. The borrowings under the 2018 Credit Facility accrue interest at a spread over either the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) or the Base Rate. We also pay a commitment fee on the unused balance of the facility. Borrowing spreads as well as commitment fees are determined based on the debt rating for senior unsecured debt of the Company, as determined by Moody&#8217;s and Standard &amp; Poor&#8217;s. The spread over LIBOR ranges from </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>0.875 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>1.500 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> per annum and commitment fees range from </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>0.075 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>0.200 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> per annum. There is a financial covenant in the 2018 Credit Facility that requires us to maintain a total debt to total capitalization ratio of less than or equal to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>50 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. The 2018 Credit Facility contains additional terms, conditions, restrictions and covenants that we believe are usual and customary in unsecured debt arrangements for companies of similar size and credit quality, including a limitation that priority debt (as defined in the credit agreement) may not exceed </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>17.5 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> of the net worth of the Company. As of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, there were </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>no</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> borrowings or letters of credit outstanding, leaving </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$750.0 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> available to borrow under the 2018 Credit Facility. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">As of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we had </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>two</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> outstanding letters of credit with banks, in the amounts of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$24.8 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$2.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">As of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we also had a </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$20.0 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> unsecured standalone line of credit facility, for the purpose of obtaining the issuance of international letters of credit, bank guarantees, and performance bonds. Of the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$20.0 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$14.3 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> of financial guarantees were outstanding as of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.  </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The applicable agreements for all unsecured debt contain additional terms, conditions and restrictions that we believe are usual and customary in unsecured debt arrangements for companies that are similar in size and credit quality.&#160;&#160;At </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">we were in compliance with all debt covenants</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.</span></div><span></span>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for information about short-term and long-term debt arrangements, which includes amounts of borrowings under each line of credit, note payable, commercial paper issue, bonds indenture, debenture issue, own-share lending arrangements and any other contractual agreement to repay funds, and about the underlying arrangements, rationale for a classification as long-term, including repayment terms, interest rates, collateral provided, restrictions on use of assets and activities, whether or not in compliance with debt covenants, and other matters important to users of the financial statements, such as the effects of refinancing and noncompliance with debt covenants.</p></div>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_LineOfCredit">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The carrying value as of the balance sheet date of the current and noncurrent portions of long-term obligations drawn from a line of credit, which is a bank's commitment to make loans up to a specific amount. Examples of items that might be included in the application of this element may consist of letters of credit, standby letters of credit, and revolving credit arrangements, under which borrowings can be made up to a maximum amount as of any point in time conditional on satisfaction of specified terms before, as of and after the date of drawdowns on the line. Includes short-term obligations that would normally be classified as current liabilities but for which (a) postbalance sheet date issuance of a long term obligation to refinance the short term obligation on a long term basis, or (b) the enterprise has entered into a financing agreement that clearly permits the enterprise to refinance the short-term obligation on a long term basis and the following conditions are met (1) the agreement does not expire within 1 year and is not cancelable by the lender except for violation of an objectively determinable provision, (2) no violation exists at the BS date, and (3) the lender has entered into the financing agreement is expected to be financially capable of honoring the agreement.</p></div>

Cash equivalents, excluding items classified as marketable securities, include short-term, highly liquid Investments that are both readily convertible to known amounts of cash, and so near their maturity that they present minimal risk of changes in value because of changes in interest rates. <th class="th" colspan="1">6 Months Ended</th>

<tr><th class="th"><div>Mar. 31, 2020</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_BusinessCombinationsAbstract', window );"><strong>Business Combinations [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_BusinessCombinationDisclosureTextBlock', window );">BUSINESS COMBINATIONS</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:none;">NOTE 3 BUSINESS COMBINATIONS</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Fiscal Year 2019 Acquisitions</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">On August 21, 2019, we completed an acquisition of an unaffiliated company, DrillScan Energy SAS and its subsidiaries ("DrillScan"), which is now a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, for total consideration of approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$32.7 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, which includes </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$17.7 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> of contingent consideration. The fair value of the total assets acquired, and liabilities assumed, as of the acquisition date, were </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$36.3 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$3.6 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, including goodwill of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$14.9 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. Of the total assets acquired, </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$19.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> was allocated to identifiable intangible assets. DrillScan is a leading provider of proprietary drilling engineering software, well engineering services and training for the oil and gas industry. The operations of DrillScan are included in the H&amp;P Technologies reportable business segment. The acquisition of DrillScan was accounted for as a business combination in accordance with FASB ASC 805, Business Combinations, which requires the assets acquired and liabilities assumed to be recorded at their acquisition date fair values. In accordance with GAAP, an entity is allowed a reasonable period of time (not to exceed one year) to obtain the information necessary to identify and measure the fair value of the assets acquired and liabilities assumed in a business combination.&#160;This acquisition is still within this measurement period, and as a result, the acquisition date fair values we have recorded for the assets acquired and liabilities assumed are subject to change as a result of new information identified. During the three and six months ended March 31, 2020, as a result of new information identified related to the acquisition of DrillScan, the acquisition date fair value of the contingent consideration and goodwill increased by approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$1.2 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">On November 1, 2018, we completed an acquisition of an unaffiliated company, Angus Jamieson Consulting (&#8220;AJC&#8221;), which is now a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, for total consideration of approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$3.4 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. AJC is a software-based training and consultancy company based in Inverness, Scotland and is widely recognized as an industry leader in wellbore positioning. The operations of AJC are included in the H&amp;P Technologies reportable segment. The acquisition of AJC has been accounted for as a business combination in accordance with FASB ASC 805, Business Combinations, which requires the assets acquired and liabilities assumed to be recorded at their acquisition date fair values. The allocation of the purchase price includes goodwill of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$3.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.</span></div><span></span>
</td>

I</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">ntangible amortization is estimated to be approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$3.6 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> for the remainder of </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">fiscal year </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$7.2 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> for fiscal years </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2021</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2022</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$6.5 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> for fiscal year </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2023</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$6.4 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> for fiscal year </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2024</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Impairments</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">Consistent with our policy, we test goodwill annually for impairment in the fourth quarter of our fiscal year, or more frequently if there are indicators that goodwill might be impaired. Due to the market conditions described in </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">Note 5&#8212;Property, Plant and Equipment</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">, we concluded that goodwill and intangible assets might be impaired and tested the H&amp;P Technologies reporting unit, where the goodwill balance is allocated and the intangible assets are recorded, for recoverability.  This resulted in a goodwill only non-cash </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">impairment charge of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$38.3 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> recorded in Asset Impairment Charge on the Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations during the three and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">six months ended March 31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">The recoverable amount of the H&amp;P Technologies segment as a reporting unit is determined based on a fair value calculation which uses cash flow projections based on the Company&#8217;s financial budgets approved by the board of directors covering a five-year period, and a discount rate of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"><span>14 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">. Cash flows beyond that five-year period have been extrapolated using the fifth-year data with no implied growth factor. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The recoverable amount of the intangible assets tested for impairment within the H&amp;P Technologies reporting unit is determined based on undiscounted cash flow projections using the Company&#8217;s financial budgets approved by the board of directors covering a five-year period, and extrapolated for the remaining weighted average useful lives of the intangible assets.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:0px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br/></span></div>The most significant assumptions used in our cash flow model include timing on awards of future contracts, commercial pricing terms, utilization, discount rate, and the terminal value. These assumptions are classified as Level 3 inputs by ASC Topic 820 Fair Value Measurement and Disclosures as they are based upon unobservable inputs and primarily rely on management assumptions and forecasts. Although we believe the assumptions used in our analysis and the probability-weighted average of expected future cash flows are reasonable and appropriate, different assumptions and estimates could materially impact the analysis and our resulting conclusion.<span></span>

lease assets &#8212; referred to as &#8220;lessees&#8221; &#8212; to recognize on the balance sheet the assets and liabilities for the rights and obligations created by those leases with lease terms of more than 12 months. Lessor accounting remains substantially similar to current U.S. GAAP. In addition, disclosures of leasing activities are to be expanded to include qualitative along with specific quantitative information. ASU No. 2016-02 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2018, including interim periods within those fiscal years. <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_IncomeLossFromDiscontinuedOperationsNetOfTaxAttributableToReportingEntity">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Amount after tax of income (loss) from a discontinued operation attributable to the parent. <tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_RevenueFromContractWithCustomerAbstract', window );"><strong>Revenue from Contract with Customer [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_RevenueFromContractWithCustomerTextBlock', window );">REVENUE FROM CONTRACTS WITH CUSTOMERS</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:none;">NOTE 11 REVENUE FROM CONTRACTS WITH CUSTOMERS</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:none;"> </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Contract Drilling Services Revenue</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Due to the continued decline in the price of oil, our customers have reduced their drilling activity and we have received rig release notifications for rigs under term and well-to-well contracts. The releases for rigs under term contracts result in early termination compensation owed to us, while releases for rigs under well-to-well contracts given outside the notification window per the contract result in notification fees owed to us. During the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">three months ended March 31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, early termination revenue associated with term contracts was approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$8.2 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$1.2 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$8.3 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> for both the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">six months ended March 31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. During the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">three months ended March 31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, notification fee revenue related to well-to-well contracts was approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$2.2 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.3 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$2.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.3 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> for the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">six months ended March 31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively. Subsequent to March 31, 2020, we have received additional rig release notifications, which will result in additional early termination and notification fee revenue. Refer to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Note 18&#8212;Subsequent Events</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">As a result of the depressed market conditions and negative outlook for the near term, certain of our customers have opted to renegotiate existing drilling contracts. During the three months ended March 31, 2020, we agreed to certain price concessions on some of our existing drilling contracts; however, the total impact on current and future periods is not significant. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Contract Costs</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We had capitalized fulfillment costs of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$9.9 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$13.9 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> as of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">September&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Remaining Performance Obligations</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The total aggregate transaction price allocated to the unsatisfied performance obligations, commonly referred to as backlog, as of&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#160;was approximately&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$837.6 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, of which approximately&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$413.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#160;is expected to be recognized during the remainder of fiscal year </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">,&#160;approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$312.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> during fiscal year </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2021</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, and approximately&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$112.4 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#160;in fiscal year </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2022</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and thereafter. These amounts do not include anticipated contract renewals. Additionally, contracts that currently contain month-to-month terms are represented in our backlog as </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>one</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> month of unsatisfied performance obligations. Our contracts are subject to cancellation or modification at the election of the customer; however, due to the level of capital deployed by our customers on underlying projects, we have not been materially adversely affected by contract cancellations or modifications in the past. We do not have material long-term contracts related to our H&amp;P Technologies segment.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Contract Assets and Liabilities</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The following tables summarize the balances of our contract assets and <tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure of revenue from contract with customer to transfer good or service and to transfer nonfinancial asset. Includes, but is not limited to, disaggregation of revenue, credit loss recognized from contract with customer, judgment and change in judgment related to contract with customer, and asset recognized from cost incurred to obtain or fulfill contract with customer. Excludes insurance and lease contracts.</p></div>

<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>

<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock', window );">Interim Financial Information</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Interim Financial Information</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The accompanying Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) and applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;) pertaining to interim financial information.&#160;Accordingly, these interim financial statements do not include all information or footnote disclosures required by GAAP for complete financial statements and, therefore, should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and notes thereto in our </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> Annual Report on Form 10-K and other current filings with the SEC.&#160;&#160;In the opinion of management, all adjustments, consisting of those of a normal recurring nature, necessary to present fairly the results of the periods presented have been included.&#160;The results of operations for the interim periods presented may not necessarily be indicative of the results to be expected for the full year. </span></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock', window );">Principles of Consolidation</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Principles of Consolidation</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The unaudited consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Helmerich &amp; Payne, Inc. and its domestic and foreign subsidiaries.&#160;Consolidation of a subsidiary begins when the Company obtains control over the subsidiary and ceases when the Company loses control of the subsidiary. Specifically, income and expenses of a subsidiary acquired or disposed of during the fiscal year are included in the unaudited condensed consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income (loss) from the date the Company gains control until the date when the Company ceases to control the subsidiary. All significant intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</span></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_CashAndCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndCashEquivalentsPolicy', window );">Cash, Cash Equivalents, and Restricted Cash</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Cash, Cash Equivalents, and Restricted Cash</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Cash and cash equivalents include cash on hand, demand deposits with banks and all highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less.&#160;Approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$294.6 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> of cash and cash equivalents resides in accounts in the United States and the remaining </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$41.5 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> are in other countries. Our cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments are subject to potential credit risk, and certain of our cash accounts carry balances greater than the federally insured limits.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We had restricted cash of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$44.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$34.2 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> at </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$35.0 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$41.8 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> at </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">September&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively. Of the total at </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">September&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$1.9 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$3.0 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, is related to the acquisition of drilling technology companies,&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$2.0 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> as of both fiscal period ends is from the additional capitalization of our wholly-owned captive insurance company, </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$39.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$30.0 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, represents an additional amount management has elected to restrict for the purpose of potential insurance claims in our wholly-owned captive insurance companies, and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$1.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> at </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> is for other restricted purposes.&#160; The restricted amounts are primarily invested in federally insured deposit accounts. </span></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock', window );">Leases</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">Leases</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We lease various offices, warehouses, equipment and vehicles. Rental contracts are typically made for fixed periods of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>1</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>15 years</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> but may have extension options. Lease terms are negotiated on an individual basis and contain a wide range of different terms and conditions. The lease agreements do not impose any covenants, but leased assets may not be used as security for borrowing purposes.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Up until the end of fiscal year 2019, leases of property, plant and equipment were classified as either finance or operating leases. Payments made under operating leases (net of any incentives received from the lessor) were charged to the income statement on a straight-line basis over the period of the lease (&#8220;levelized lease cost&#8221;).</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Beginning October 1, 2019, leases are recognized as a right-of-use asset and a corresponding liability within accrued liabilities and other non-current liabilities at the date at which the leased asset is available for use by the Company. Each lease payment is allocated between the liability and finance cost. The finance cost is recognized over the lease period to produce a constant periodic rate of interest on the remaining balance of the liability for each period. The right-of-use asset is depreciated over the shorter of the asset's useful life and the lease term on a straight-line basis for finance type leases and as the difference between the levelized lease cost and the finance cost for operating leases. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:13px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Assets and liabilities arising from a lease are initially measured on a present value basis. Lease liabilities include the net present value of the following lease payments: </span></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:96px;"/><td/></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Fixed payments (including in-substance fixed payments), less any lease incentives receivable</span></div></td></tr></table><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:96px;"/><td/></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Variable lease payments that are based on an index or a rate</span></div></td></tr></table><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:96px;"/><td/></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Amounts expected to be payable by the lessee under residual value guarantees</span></div></td></tr></table><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:96px;"/><td/></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The exercise price of a purchase option if the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise that option, and</span></div></td></tr></table><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:96px;"/><td/></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Payments of penalties for terminating the lease, if the lease term reflects the lessee exercising that option.</span></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The lease payments are discounted using the interest rate implicit in the lease. If that rate cannot be determined, the lessee&#8217;s incremental borrowing rate is used, which is the rate that the lessee would have to pay to borrow the funds necessary to obtain an asset of similar value in a similar economic environment with similar terms and conditions.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:13px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Right-of-use assets are measured at cost and are comprised of the following:</span></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:96px;"/><td/></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The amount of the initial measurement of lease liability</span></div></td></tr></table><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:96px;"/><td/></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Any lease payments made at or before the commencement date less any lease incentives received</span></div></td></tr></table><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; Short-term leases are leases with a lease term of 12 months or less. Low-value assets are comprised of IT-equipment and office furniture.</span></div>In determining the lease term, management considers all facts and circumstances that create an economic incentive to exercise an extension option, or not exercise a termination option. Extension options (or periods after termination options) are only included in the lease term if the lease is reasonably certain to be extended (or not terminated). The assessment is reviewed if a significant event or a significant change in circumstances occurs and is within the control of the lessee.<span></span>

<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_SelfInsuranceReservePolicyTextBlock', window );">Self-Insurance</a></td>
<td class="text">&lt;div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Self-Insurance&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We self-insure a significant portion of expected losses relating to workers&amp;#8217; compensation, general liability and automobile liability. Generally, deductibles range from &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$1 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$10 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; per occurrence depending on the coverage and whether a claim occurs outside or inside of the United States. Insurance is purchased over deductibles to reduce our exposure to catastrophic events. Estimates are recorded for incurred outstanding liabilities for workers&amp;#8217; compensation, general liability claims and claims that are incurred but not reported. Estimates are based on adjusters' estimates, historical experience and statistical methods commonly used within the insurance industry that we believe are reliable.&amp;#160;We have also engaged a third-party actuary to perform a review of our domestic casualty losses as well as losses in our captive insurance companies.&amp;#160;Nonetheless, insurance estimates include certain assumptions and management judgments regarding the frequency and severity of claims, claim development and settlement practices. Unanticipated changes in these factors may produce materially different amounts of expense that would be reported under these programs.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;<span></span>

<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_hp_InternationalDrillingOperationsPolicyPolicyTextBlock', window );">International Land Drilling Risks</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-decoration:none;">International Land Drilling Risks</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">International Land drilling operations may significantly contribute to our revenues and net operating income.&#160;There can be no assurance that we will be able to successfully conduct such operations, and a failure to do so may have an adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations, and cash flows.&#160;Also, the success of our international land operations will be subject to numerous contingencies, some of which are beyond management&#8217;s control.&#160;These contingencies include general and regional economic conditions, fluctuations in currency exchange rates, modified exchange controls, changes in international regulatory requirements and international employment issues, risk of expropriation of real and personal property and the burden of complying with foreign laws.&#160;Additionally, in the event that extended labor strikes occur or a country experiences significant political, economic or social instability, we could experience shortages in labor and/or material and supplies necessary to operate some of our drilling rigs, thereby potentially causing an adverse material effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations. In Argentina, while our dayrate is denominated in U.S. dollars, we are paid in Argentine pesos.&#160;The Argentine branch of one of our second-tier subsidiaries remits U.S. dollars to its U.S. parent by converting the Argentine pesos into U.S. dollars through the Argentine Foreign Exchange Market and repatriating the U.S. dollars.&#160;Argentina also has a history of implementing currency controls which restrict the conversion and repatriation of U.S. dollars, including controls that were implemented in September 2019 and are presently in effect. As a result of these currency controls, our ability to remit funds from our Argentine subsidiary to its U.S. parent has been limited. As of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, our cash balance in Argentina was </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$33.7 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">In the past the Argentine government has also instituted price controls on crude oil, diesel and gasoline prices and instituted an exchange rate freeze in connection with those prices. These price controls and an exchange rate freeze could be instituted again in the future. Argentina&#8217;s economy is considered highly inflationary, which is defined as cumulative inflation rates exceeding </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>100 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> in the most recent three-year period based on inflation data published by the respective governments.&#160;Nonetheless, all of our foreign subsidiaries use the U.S. dollar as the functional currency and local currency monetary assets and liabilities are remeasured into U.S. dollars with gains and losses resulting from foreign currency transactions included in current results of operations.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">For the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">three and six</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we experienced aggregate foreign currency </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">losses</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$3.4 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$2.8 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively. For the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">three and six</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we recorded aggregate foreign currency losses of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.7 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$4.6 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively. In the future, we may incur larger currency devaluations, foreign exchange restrictions or other difficulties repatriating U.S. dollars from Argentina or elsewhere, which could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Because of the impact of local laws, our future operations in certain areas may be conducted through entities in which local citizens own interests and through entities (including joint ventures) in which we hold only a minority interest or pursuant to arrangements under which we conduct operations under contract to local entities.&#160;While we believe that neither operating through such entities nor pursuant to such arrangements would have a material adverse effect on our operations or revenues, there can be no assurance that we will in all cases be able to structure or restructure our operations to conform to local law (or the administration thereof) on terms acceptable to us.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Although we attempt to minimize the potential impact of such risks by operating in more than </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>one</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> geographical area, during the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">three and six</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>8.2 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>8.0 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, of our operating revenues were generated from international locations in our contract drilling business compared to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>7.1 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>8.1 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> during the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">three and six</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively. During the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">three and six</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>66.4 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>76.2 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, of operating revenues from international locations were from operations in South America compared to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>93.9 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>90.9 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> during the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">three and six</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively. Substantially all of the South American operating revenues were from Argentina and Colombia. The future occurrence of one or more international events arising from the types of risks described above could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.</span></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
